column1: # 847-850 restored to the Latin's line order (cum facere instituas is 849). 862-863, 865 secondaries accepted.

column2: Just as, for the soothing liquor of marjoram and of myrrh {{NOTE: amaracinum and stacte, perfumed oils of marjoram and of myrrh}}
when you set about making them, it is right first to seek,
as far as you may and can find it, an odorless olive oil,
pliant with soft, brittle with crumbling, hollow with porous body,
all these must be kept apart from the beginnings, {{NOTE: principia, Lucretius's other name for the primordia; rendered "beginnings"}}
if we wish to set beneath things foundations immortal,
on which the whole of their safety may rest;
so that all things do not return utterly to nothing for you.
Now all the things we see to have sense, whatever they are,
beginnings. Nor do plain facts refute this
are united as they must be for living things to be born.
For the positions of the beginnings are dissolved,
since they are not made out of any bodies of beginnings,
